hints.title: Find the centres and radii
hints.body: Read each centre and radius from the circle equations. Use Pythagoras to find the distance between the centres.

hints.pause: Sketch the circles and label the distance between their centres.

hints.title: Put the points as far apart as possible
hints.body: Join the centres and extend the line through both circles. Put the two points at the outer ends of this line, on the far sides of the circles.
hints.recap: The whole distance consists of a radius, the centre-to-centre distance and another radius.
hints.pitfall: Use the far sides of the circles; points facing each other would be closer.
hints.pause: Add the three lengths and simplify your answer.

recall.reminder: The whole distance consists of a radius, the centre-to-centre distance and another radius.

solution:
1. Read the circles. Their centres are A=(2,1) and B=(4,−5), both with radius 4. The centre distance is AB=22+(−6)2=210.

2. Bound the separation. The route from P through A and B to Q has length 4+AB+4, so PQ≤8+210.

3. Attain the bound. Put P on the extension of BA beyond A and Q on the extension of AB beyond B. Then P,A,B,Q are collinear in that order and both points lie on their circles. The maximum is 8+210. Answer F.
knowledgePattern: Maximise separation between circle points using centre distance and both radii
